problem:
The basis $B$ of ${R}^{3}$ and the matrix $[\,T\,]_{B}$ of the linear transformation $T:{R}^{3}\to {R}^{3}$ relative to $B$ are given by

$$
B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ 0 \\ 0\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ 2 \\ 2\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 3 \\ -1\end{aligned}]},\,[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}a & -1 & 2 \\ 6 & b & -2 \\ -4 & -2 & c\end{aligned}].
$$

What is the value of $\,a+b+c,\,$ given that  

$$
T({b}_{1})=[\begin{aligned}-4 \\ 0 \\ 16\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}-1 \\ -6 \\ 2\end{aligned}],\,T({b}_{3})=[\begin{aligned}4 \\ 2 \\ -6\end{aligned}].
$$

examples.problem:
The basis $\mathcal{B}$ of $\mathbb{R}^3$ and the matrix $[\,\mathbf{T}\,]_{\mathcal{B}}$ of the linear transformation $\mathbf{T}: \mathbb{R}^3 \rightarrow \mathbb{R}^3$ relative to $\mathcal{B}$ are given by

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14066994/assets/6efd50facaf6c5a4d4b536eaa194bbfcf240cf30804bb13a7a6ac479adf6d864.png)

What is the value of $\,a+b+c,\,$ given that  

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14066994/assets/1d585e7b839d1e569693d7489c23e47761e2f96bdf114ee96f4b287aa68d7fa4.png)
examples.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $\mathcal{B}$ as $\{ \mathbf{b}_1,\mathbf{b}_2,\mathbf{b}_3 \}.$ The $\mathcal{B}$-matrix for $\mathbf{T}$ is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_1),$ $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_2),$ and $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_3)$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{B}.$

To find the coordinates of $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_1),$ $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_2),$ and $\mathbf{T}(\mathbf{b}_3)$ relative to the basis $\mathcal{B}$, we consider the matrix
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14066994/assets/318cfa577ad284a0b606eb58232ee0276deedcbd446357e7f5b4c690b46b2208.png)

Now, we reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination. Then, on the right-hand side, we will obtain the $\mathcal{B}$-matrix for $\mathbf{T}\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 & -9 & 7 & 10 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 0 & -2 & -10 \\ 0 & 0 & 4 & 4 & 0 & 8\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{3}:=\frac{1}{4}{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 & -9 & 7 & 10 \\ 0 & 1 & -3 & 0 & -2 & -10 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{3}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & -3 & 0 & -9 & 7 & 10 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 & -2 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}+3{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 0 & 0 & 1 & -2 \\ 0 & 1 & 0 & 3 & -2 & -4 \\ 0 & 0 & 1 & 1 & 0 & 2\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain
![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14066994/assets/5181a3a65f33553fad4c1ebf5ac81e9c2e3957576ac0501b953afcbf8c09349d.png)

Finally, $a=1,$ $b=-2,$ $c=-2$ and 

$$
a+b+c = 1+(-2)+(-2) = -3.
$$

feedback.problem:
Let $B$ be a basis of ${R}^{2}$ and let $T:{R}^{2}\to {R}^{2}$ be a linear transformation. Find $[\,T\,]_{B}$, given that

$\,$ $T({b}_{1})=[\begin{aligned}2 \\ -5\end{aligned}],\,$ $T({b}_{2})=[\begin{aligned}3 \\ 4\end{aligned}],\,$ and $\,B={[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -3\end{aligned}],[\begin{aligned}1 \\ -2\end{aligned}]}.$
feedback.worked_solution:
Let's denote the vectors of $B$ as ${{b}_{1},{b}_{2}}.$ The $B$-matrix for $T$ is a matrix whose columns are the coordinates of the vectors $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B.$

To find the coordinates of $T({b}_{1})$ and $T({b}_{2})$ relative to the basis $B$, we consider the matrix

$$
M=[\begin{aligned}| & | & | & | \\ {b}_{1} & {b}_{2} & T({b}_{1}) & T({b}_{2}) \\ | & | & | & |\end{aligned}].
$$

Now, we reduce the left-hand side to reduced row echelon form using Gaussian elimination. Then, on the right-hand side, we will obtain the $B$-matrix for $T:$

$$
\begin{aligned}M & =[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ -3 & -2 & -5 & 4\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{2}:={R}_{2}+3{R}_{1}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 1 & 2 & 3 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 13\end{aligned}] &  & \begin{aligned}{R}_{1}:={R}_{1}-{R}_{2}\end{aligned} \\  & ∼[\begin{aligned}1 & 0 & 1 & -10 \\ 0 & 1 & 1 & 13\end{aligned}]\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we obtain

$$
[\,T\,]_{B}=[\begin{aligned}1 & -10 \\ 1 & 13\end{aligned}].
$$
